questions.text: Change one letter of ROME to make the place where you live.
questions.why: Change the R of ROME to H and you get HOME.

Tom's mother has three children. The first is called April, the second is called May. What is the third called?
questions.why: It's Tom's mother, so Tom is her third child.

questions.text: I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish. What am I?
questions.why: A map shows cities, forests and water without any of the real houses, trees or fish.
The gaps go up by one each time (2, 3, 4, 5), so the next gap is 6: 15 + 6 = 21.

questions.text: A woman has two coins that add up to 30p. One of them is not a 20p. What are the coins?
questions.why: Only one of the coins is not a 20p; the other one is, so the pair is 20p + 10p.

questions.text: What is the smallest number that is divisible by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?
questions.why: 60 = 4 × 3 × 5, which covers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 (6 = 2 × 3), and nothing smaller does.

questions.text: A lily pad doubles in size every day and covers a pond in 30 days. On which day did it cover half the pond?
questions.why: It doubles every day, so it covered half the pond the day before it covered all of it: day 29.

questions.text: 'Divorced, beheaded, died, divorced, beheaded, survived.' How many of Henry's wives outlived him?
questions.why: Catherine Parr 'survived', but divorced Anne of Cleves also outlived Henry, dying in 1557, so that makes two.

questions.text: The Great Pyramid was finished around 2560 BC and the Colosseum in AD 80. With no year zero, how many years apart were they finished?
questions.why: 2560 + 80 = 2640, minus 1 because there was no year zero, gives 2,639.

questions.text: How many squares are there on a chessboard? Not just the small ones.
questions.why: Count the squares of each size from 1×1 to 8×8: 64 + 49 + 36 + 25 + 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 204.
